WorkLog

The WorkLog control displays the progress of multiple jobs. Each job is a WorkItem with its own label, status, item counts and running time.

Properties and Methods

  • Tasks: The LockedList<WorkItem> shown by the control. WorkItem objects belong in this list rather than Children.
  • WorkItem.Run / Wait / Complete / Error: Changes the state of a job. The stopwatch starts when a job runs and stops when it is no longer running.
  • ShowStatus / ShowTime / ShowItemCount / ShowProgressBar: Controls which details are displayed for each job.
  • FollowRunning / VisibleStartIndex: FollowRunning keeps a running job visible. Set it to false to choose the starting row with VisibleStartIndex.
  • GetItemByName: Finds a job using its ElmName.

C# Example

Create the control and add it to the page's Children or the window's Elements collection. The Controls Overview lists the namespaces used by these examples.

Output Example

Notes

ElmName identifies the job; Label is the text displayed to the user.

The list supports snapshot rendering, but WorkItem itself is mutable. Update job state on the UI thread while the WorkLog is attached.

WorkLog does not execute jobs or handle their exceptions. Your application is responsible for running the work and updating the status.

The common position, color, visibility and lifetime settings are inherited from UIElement. While attached to a running window, update the control on the UI thread.
